```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(SpatialFeatureExperiment)

require(colorout)

options("styler.addins_style_transformer" = "biocthis::bioc_style()")

library(parallelly)
options(parallelly.supportsMulticore.disableOn="")
options(parallelly.fork.enable=TRUE)
library(BiocParallel)
options(bphost="localhost")
library(parallel)

## ggplot defaults
#theme_set(theme_bw()+theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14), axis.title.x = element_text(size = 16), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14), axis.title.y = element_text(size =16), plot.title = element_text(size = 20,hjust=0.5), strip.text = element_text(size=18), legend.text = element_text(size=10), legend.title = element_text(size=11,hjust=0.5)))
```

## read in filtered SPE
```{r}
lcx <- readRDS("processed-data/02_QC/01b-spe_controlOutliers_and_tinynuc_and_giantLCmarkerlessNuclei_filtered.RDS")
```

## get all (targeting) genes
## get lognorm counts for running standard PCA / UMAP
```{r}
genetargeting <- grep(rownames(lcx),pattern="Unassigned|NegCon|Deprecated",value=T,invert=T)
lcx <- lcx[genetargeting,]

lcx <- computeLibraryFactors(lcx)
lcx <- logNormCounts(lcx)

## Banksy's documentation generally uses NON-log normalization, so we might as well get that too while we're at it.
assay(lcx,"normcounts") <- normalizeCounts(lcx,log=FALSE)
```

## run PCA on log counts using all (targeting) genes
```{r}
set.seed(42)
lcx <- scater::runPCA(lcx,subset_row=genetargeting,assay.type="logcounts",BPPARAM=MulticoreParam(4))

set.seed(42)
lcx <- scater::runUMAP(lcx,n_threads=6) ## n threads requires RcppHNSW

rastumap <- as.data.table(reducedDim(lcx,"UMAP"),keep.rownames=T)
rastumap <- merge.data.table(rastumap,as.data.table(colData(lcx),keep.rownames=T),by="rn")


```

## repeat as above using raw counts with correspondence analysis (CA) as executed via corral:: . this is described in https://bioconductor.org/books/3.19/OSCA.advanced/dimensionality-reduction-redux.html#count-based-dimensionality-reduction

OSCA explains the underlying procedure for CA for raw cuont data:
"For count matrices, correspondence analysis (CA) is a natural approach to dimensionality reduction. In this procedure, we compute an expected value for each entry in the matrix based on the per-gene abundance and size factors. Each count is converted into a standardized residual in a manner analogous to the calculation of the statistic in Pearson’s chi-squared tests, i.e., subtraction of the expected value and division by its square root. An SVD is then applied on this matrix of residuals to obtain the necessary low-dimensional coordinates for each cell. 

The major advantage of CA is that it avoids difficulties with the mean-variance relationship upon transformation [...] If two cells have the same expression profile but differences in their total counts, CA will return the same expected location for both cells; this avoids artifacts observed in PCA on log-transformed counts [...] However, CA is more sensitive to overdispersion in the random noise due to the nature of its standardization. This may cause some problems in some datasets where the CA factors may be driven by a few genes with random expression rather than the underlying biological structure."

```{r}
## When run on a summarizedExperiment, returns a another with the embeddings (PCv from the full corral output) in the reducedDim slot "corral" (default)

lcx <- corral::corral_sce(lcx,subset_row=genetargeting,whichmat = "counts")

## run UMAP on the CA matrix
set.seed(42)
lcx <- runUMAP(lcx,dimred="corral",name="UMAP_CA",n_threads=6)

# save the CA and both UMAP matrices bound to cell-level metadata as a table to plot from without needing to load up the whole SPE
setnames(rastumap,c("UMAP1","UMAP2"),paste0(c("UMAP1","UMAP2"),"_PCA"))

rastumap.co <- as.data.table(reducedDim(lcx,"UMAP_CA"),keep.rownames=T)
setnames(rastumap.co,c("UMAP1","UMAP2"),paste0(c("UMAP1","UMAP2"),"_CA"))

rastumap <- merge.data.table(rastumap,rastumap.co,by="rn")

camat <- as.data.table(reducedDim(lcx,"corral"),keep.rownames=T)
## ^ this doesnt have colnames so add
setnames(camat,c(2:ncol(camat)),paste0("CA_dim",c(1:(ncol(camat)-1))))

rastumap <- merge.data.table(rastumap,camat,by="rn")

## save for plotting
fwrite(rastumap,"processed-data/02_QC/02a-genetarg-PCAUMAP_rawct_and_Corral_andCorralUMAP_w_metadata.txt.gz",sep='\t',quote=F)

# clean up enviro
rm(rastumap,rastumap.co,camat)
gc()

```

## APOE encoding was a continual pain with the visium data so just fix them here and be done with it.
```{r}
lcx$APOE <- gsub(lcx$APOE,pattern=" ",replacement="")
lcx$APOE[lcx$APOE=="E4/E4"] <- "E4hom" 
lcx$APOE[lcx$APOE=="E3/E4"] <- "E4het" 
lcx$APOE[lcx$APOE=="E2/E3"] <- "E2het"
lcx$APOE[lcx$APOE=="E2/E2"] <- "E2hom"
# unique(lcx$APOE)
# [1] "E4hom" "E2hom" "E4het" "E2het"
```

## save SPE with normalized counts, dimreds, and demos
```{r}
saveRDS(lcx,"processed-data/02_QC/02b-spe_filtered_genetargonly_log-and-nonlog-norms.RDS")
```
